motivation: Stuck is not failing. Stuck is your brain building a new road.
Nobody is born knowing two pointers. Everyone who knows it once didn't.
Solve it slowly today; tomorrow you'll solve it fast.
One problem a day is 365 problems a year.
Brute force first. Every elegant solution started as an ugly one.
Interviewers want to hear you think, not watch you be perfect.
Wrong answer? Good. Now you know one way it doesn't work.
Draw it before you code it. Paper never throws a segfault.
Ten minutes stuck is learning. Two hours stuck has earned you a hint.
Today's hard problem is next month's warm-up.
A little every day beats a lot once. Come back tomorrow.
You're not behind. You're on your own route, one station at a time.
Every pattern you learn makes ten more problems easy.
Read the constraints. They whisper the complexity you need.
The bug is never where you're looking. Breathe, look somewhere else.
One problem you understand beats three you memorised.
Off-by-one errors humble everyone. Laugh, fix, move on.
Future you, in the interview room, will thank you for this one.
Tea in one hand, logic in the other. Let's go.
Hard means unfamiliar, not impossible.
Edge cases are where good engineers are made.
Close the tab of doubt. Open the editor.
Slow progress is still progress. The train is moving.
Explain it to a rubber duck. If the duck gets it, so do you.

topicSub.arrays-hashing: The basics everything else builds on: scanning arrays and strings, two pointers, sliding windows, and hash maps for instant lookups.
topicSub.linked-list: A linked list stores data in nodes, each one linked to the next. Here you learn to add and remove nodes and rewire their links.
topicSub.stack: Stacks and queues keep data in a particular order; binary search finds an element in sorted data fast. Together they cover efficient handling and searching.
topicSub.trees: Trees are hierarchies of parent and child nodes. This is about traversing them, the depth of nodes, and how nodes relate to each other.
topicSub.graphs: Graphs show how things relate, with nodes and edges. This covers traversals (BFS, DFS) and the relationships between nodes.
topicSub.backtracking: Recursion solves a problem by calling itself on smaller pieces. Backtracking tries options one by one, and steps back when it hits a dead end.
topicSub.dp-1d: Dynamic programming stores the answers to subproblems that repeat, so nothing is computed twice and harder problems become fast.
topicSub.heap: Choosing by priority, handling overlapping intervals, and picking the right option at each step: Top-K, scheduling and merging intervals.

dsaProblems.topicsSub: Eight topics, in learning order. Each one builds on the one before.
